newsitem.title: HAITI: Canada renews commitment to keep troops in Haiti.
newsitem.headline: Canada renews commitment to keep troops in Haiti.

text.p: Canada is willing to keep troops in Haiti after the U.N. peacekeeping mission's mandate expires but they will not serve alone, Canadian officials said on Wednesday.

Canadian Minister of Foreign Cooperation Don Boudria met Haiti's President Rene Preval on Wednesday to discuss the commitment of Canadian troops after the scheduled departure of U.N. peacekeepers on July 31.

"We Canadians are ready to stay in Haiti in the months following the deadline," Boudria told a news conference at the National Palace, echoing an announcement made by Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy last month.
However, ministry spokesman Jacques Lefevre said the Canadians would not stay on as the only foreign contingent. "It would have to be a multi-national mission," he said.
U.N. sources say it is highly unlikely another U.N. peacekeeping mission would be approved by the Security Council.
Canadian diplomats have said Canadian peacekeeping support in Haiti, which is estimated to cost $8 million a month, is a favour to the United States.
About 700 Canadian soldiers currently patrol Haiti's streets alongside 500 Pakistani troops who are funded by the United States.
There are also about 300 U.S., French, Canadian and Algerian police officers training the Haitian National Police under U.N. auspices.
